newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe industrials end weaker on new issues.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe industrials end weaker on new issues.

text.p: Zimbabwean industrial shares ended the weaker on Friday with brokers saying the market had gone to sleep as players digested new issues made this week and waited for others due later in the month.
The key industrial index lost 34.41 points to close at 10,478.51. It dropped 221.28 points on the week.
"The new issues are sending the market to sleep while everyone digests them and waits for the ones that are coming up soon," one broker said.

The new issues include manufacturing and marketing group Randalls Holdings Ltd which is planning to raise Z$60 million through an offer of 50 million shares, about 24 percent of its total share capital, to investors.
"I would not expect much major strength in the market until in two months' time when the issues are over," he added.

On the Zimbabwe Stock Exchange on Friday, bankers Barclays, blue-chip hotel and beverages conglomerate Delta, textilers Spinweave, clothing and furniture retailer Tedco, tobacco group TSL and newly-listed TZI traded unchanged in large turnover.

Among the day's winners, publishing group Zimpapers leapt 150 cents to 3,650, horticulture group Ariston rose 100 cents to 2,300, sugar producer Hippo gained 50 cents to 1,550 and engineering firm Gullivers added 35 cents to 350.

Among the losers, hotel and supermarket group Meikles at 2,600, cement producer Porthold at 1,700, clothing retailer Edgars at 4,600 and cement-maker Circem at 650 all dropped 100 cents while Alloys shed 25 cents to 600.
Minings were mixed to firmer and more active than of late despite an softer bullion price. Gold producer Rio Tinto rose 50 cents to 2,300 but Falgold lost 10 cents to 70.
The mining index edged 2.28 points up to 961.92 -- a 60.5 point gain on the week.
